chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Maʿrūf, from ʿAlī ibn Mahzīyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from some of his companions, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them: concerning
A man performing wudu (ablution) while he is wearing a turban. He said: “He should raise the turban enough to insert his finger, then wipe over the front part of his head.”

key_terms.إِصْبَعَهُ: his finger, used here to indicate a small opening
key_terms.الْعِمَامَةُ: the turban worn on the head
key_terms.مُقَدَّمِ رَأْسِهِ: the front part of his head, the place of wiping in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How should someone wipe the head in wudu (ablution) while wearing a turban?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about wudu (ablution) for a person wearing a turban. It states that the turban should be lifted enough to allow access for wiping the front part of the head, indicating that the required wiping must be done on the head itself.
